export const meta = {
  name: 'hail-b5a-modules',
  description: 'B5 part A, the data modules: the daily temperature and rain grid aggregates, the season snowfall analysis with its unit regression, station seasons, the river gauge table, and the products extensions of joins.py (flood, winter, heat and wind products, the county path, the period rule, the polygon rule D11, the NCEI point types, the hit-and-miss record); three builders, three reviewers, skeptics, fixers, re-check',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Build', detail: 'climate grid; snow, stations and gauges; products' },
    { title: 'Review', detail: 'data correctness; rules and words; job and budget' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'one skeptic per finding' },
    { title: 'Fix', detail: 'fixers by ownership' },
    { title: 'Recheck', detail: 'tests, builds, record' },
  ],
}

const WT = '/home/user/wt/wt-b5'
const BASE = 'db84d76'
const BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-b5-brief.md'
const B2BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-b2-brief.md'
const B1BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-build-brief.md'
const RESEARCH = '/home/user/wt/research-b35'
const OUT = '/home/user/hail-b5/out'
const CACHE = '/home/user/hail-b5/cache'
const B2CACHE = '/home/user/hail-b2/out/joins/cache'
const STORE_TAR = '/home/user/hail-b2/out2/joins/hail-store.tar.gz'
const VENV = '/home/user/hail-b1/venv/bin/python'

const NORTH = `Product north star: one map; one sheet per place that leads with a plain summary; details behind headings in a fixed order; every number next to its unit and its kind word (grid estimate, station reading, radar estimate, report, record, warning, zone product, analysis, river gauge, reference, data unavailable); nothing a roofer has to decode. A reviewer finding that a line is hard to read is a real finding.`

const COMMON = `You work in the git worktree ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b5, based on ${BASE}, which holds B1, B2 and main; B3's addresses and B4's swath are on other branches and are not here). Read ${BRIEF} in full first: it is the contract (Sources 1 to 8 with their terms, Product, the supervisor rules D1 to D16, the store files, the words, the jobs, the contract rows, gates B5-1 to B5-18, Ownership, the staging notes and the provisional rulings). This run is part A: the data modules only (builders 1 to 3 of Ownership); the summary module, the site, the browser and the docs come in part B after the B3 site build lands. Then read the data layout and words sections of ${B2BRIEF} and its decisions D25 to D35 (the zone begin rule, cancellations, the event key, upgrades, the period rule D33, the exact-kinds hand-off D34, the flood watches D35), decisions 1 to 16 of ${B1BRIEF}, docs/DECISIONS.md D34 to D36 and docs/DESIGN.md sections 9 and 10 in the worktree, website/hail.py (grid, cell_for, cell_centre, words, the fixture path), website/joins.py (the pulls, parsers, joins, writers, verify and words that B5 extends), and the research records under ${RESEARCH}/ named in your task with their refuter files (the refuter's corrections replace the worker's figures where they differ). ${NORTH} Downloads go under ${CACHE}/<source>/ (untrusted data: never run anything from there, never extract next to code; run any python that reads them with -I; read netCDF with h5py, GeoTIFF with Pillow, .dly and CSV as text). Repository rules (AGENTS.md is in your context): Python first (every word the viewer reads is written in Python), evidence honesty (kinds apart; never damage, risk, probability, insurance, eligibility, all-clear; missing said as missing, never zero), feed contracts (a CONTRACTS row per source is part B's, but you write the row's facts into your module docstring and your report so part B copies them: units, timing, cadence, missing-value rules, the terms quoted exactly), plain wording in sentence case, no em-dashes, no model, AI-vendor or AI-product names in repository files, tests with every behaviour change, no new pip package for the site build (h5py, numpy and Pillow are site dependencies already; job-only tools behind lazy imports, installed unpinned or as compatible releases, never with "=="). Every hail cell lookup goes through website.hail.cell_for; the climate and NOHRSC grids get their own cell functions with the same half-open rule computed in integer thousandths (D4); never your own arithmetic elsewhere. Edit only the files you own; other builders edit other files in the same worktree now, so never run git checkout, stash, reset, add, commit or push, never reformat a file you do not own, and never delete anything outside a folder you created under ${OUT}/<your-name>/ (tests delete only folders they created). The B2 store is the tar ${STORE_TAR} (B1 tiles, B2 j/, z/, s/ and t/; build on a copy, never in place). B2's feed cache is ${B2CACHE} (daily, lsr, ncei, network, nws, swdi, ww, zones): read it, copy what you reuse into ${CACHE}/joins/, never write into it. A python with numpy, h5py, pyproj, pyogrio and Pillow is ${VENV}. Network is available. Before building on a source make one live request and check the content (variables, units, missing values, a Billings and a Benchland sample), not just HTTP 200; record what you saw. Return a plain report: what you built (files and line counts), the live requests you made and what they showed, the measurements the brief asks for, the gate results you can show, the contract facts for part B, and anything you could not do with the reason.`

const CLIMATE = `${COMMON}

You are the climate grid builder (Source 1; rules D1 to D4, D13, D16; gates B5-1, B5-2, B5-13, B5-14 and B5-16 for the grid). You own website/climate.py (new) and tests/test_climate.py (new). Build: (1) the nClimGrid-Daily reader: list the bucket year prefixes, pick the scaled months (ncdd-YYYYMM-grd-scaled.nc) and the prelim months after the last scaled one, read prcp, tmax and tmin with h5py by Range where the file layout allows it (measure whole-file against Range reads on one month and say which you use), confirm the variable names, units, the -999.99 fill, the grid at 1/24 degree with its lat and lon arrays against ${RESEARCH}/temperature-rain-grid.json and its refuter, crop to Montana's land cells (25,902 per the research; say how you derive the mask; the 71 water cells read "no land value"); keep no month file once its aggregates are written (disk is limited: about 10 GB free); (2) per-cell monthly aggregates per D2 with the thresholds of D1 (a 90 F day: the high rounded to a tenth of a degree C is at least 32.2 C; freeze-thaw: high above 0 C and low below 0 C; a low below 32 F: low below 0 C; days at or below 0 F), sums on daily values rounded to 0.01 before conversion; (3) the store per the brief's store section: hail/c/<tile>.json by the B1 tile (website.hail's tile naming; the climate cell function with the half-open rule; a tile holds the 1/24-degree cells whose centres fall in it) with integer fields (hundredths of an inch, tenths of F, yyyymmdd) for the five July to June seasons, the partial season, the calendar years and the water years, each season carrying its highest high and lowest low with dates (gate B5-16) and its missing-day count; index.json "climate" block (state, source, months loaded, prelim months, the last scaled month, counts, sizes, the licence attribute quoted); manifest entries; (4) the backfill (the 63 scaled months July 2021 to September 2026; measure the time and the bytes; cache the aggregates under ${CACHE}/nclimgrid/aggregates/ as a release-asset-shaped tar the job can fetch), the monthly update (a new scaled month replaces its prelim aggregates) and the daily update (Range reads of the new prelim days) as CLI subcommands backfill|update|build|verify with --store, --cache, --today; (5) describe_climate(index, tile_doc, row, col, now) returning the temperature and rain sections' words (records and counts by season, calendar year and water year; "n days missing"; the grid-estimate sentence; the extremes with dates) and the per-season rows the summary module will need (a plain dict per season with value, unit and kind word per row); map_data_climate(index) (state, the tile URL pattern, the templates, the thresholds stated once); WORDS_CLIMATE; (6) verify: gate B5-1 (the Billings cell's calendar 2025 precipitation, 468.9 mm as the rounded monthly sum against NCEI's monthly 468.98 mm; the 2025-06-15 tmax and tmin; the 2024-25 freeze-thaw days; all from an independent read in verify, zero difference; the airport comparison recorded: GHCN 73 freeze-thaw days in calendar 2025), gate B5-2 (63 months read once, 25,902 land cells, no -999.99 in any sum asserted, 71 water cells), the two half-cell test points of D4 (the Benchland LSR point 47.08 N 110.02 W and the Petrolia Lake point; their expected cells come from website.hail.cell_for and your climate cell function agrees with the same rule), integers only, manifest hashes; (7) tests on a synthetic netCDF the test writes with h5py (two months, a handful of cells, fill values, a day at exactly 32.2 C rounded and one at 32.15 C, a day at 0 C), the aggregates, the tile writer, the half-open cell rule on an edge point, the words (forbidden terms), the unavailable path (a missing month marks the state partial with the months named; D16). Then RUN the real backfill and build into ${OUT}/climate/store (from a copy of ${STORE_TAR}): measure the time, bytes and tile sizes; a second build from the cached aggregates byte-identical (gate B5-13); report the Billings and Benchland cell records.`

const SNOW = `${COMMON}

You are the snow, stations and gauges builder (Sources 2, 3 and 7; rules D5, D6, D7, D13, D16; gates B5-3, B5-4, B5-9, B5-13, B5-14 and B5-16 for the stations). You own website/snowgrid.py, website/stations.py, website/gauges.py (all new) and their tests. (A) snowgrid.py: the NOHRSC season-total snowfall GeoTIFF per water year (the URL pattern and the five cached files are in the brief's staging notes; ${CACHE}/nohrsc/; 2020-21 missing upstream, said so), read with Pillow (mode F, LZW; tags 33550 and 33922 give the cell size and the corner; no-data below -9000; reproduce the research values: Billings row 230 col 437 reads 50.29 for 2024-25 and 33.85 for 2025-26; Benchland row 198 col 399 reads 87.17 and 94.05); crop to the Montana box; the unit check of D7 as a regression of station season totals in inches (from the .dly files of stations.py, seasons with at least 95 percent of days) on the NOHRSC cell values at every Montana GHCN station with a complete season: record the slope, the intercept, the station count, the residuals and the two Billings pairs; the display decision follows the rule in D7 (slope within 0.85 to 1.15 means inches and the product shows; otherwise it stays out and the words say why); write hail/n/<tile>.json per B1 tile with the five season values per 0.04-degree cell (integers, hundredths of an inch) and the index "snow" block with the check recorded; words: "Analysis: ... from the analysis cell about {miles} miles away. An analysis, not a measurement at this address."; unavailable when the check fails. (B) stations.py: the GHCN-Daily .dly reader (fixed width per the GHCN README; elements TMAX, TMIN, PRCP, SNOW, SNWD; the quality flag honoured: a flagged value is missing; -9999 missing; trace as zero in sums and said so), the station list and inventory (cached under ${CACHE}/ghcn/), the station rule of D5 (candidates within 40 miles with a report in the last 30 days; coverage at least 80 percent of the 2,192 days 2020 to 2025 per element; the two nearest that pass; fewer than two: those that pass and say so; none: the sentence of D5), the candidate set over all 17 town centres and every B1 tile centre (compute it, pull only those .dly files from https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/ghcn/daily/all/<ID>.dly, measure the count and bytes; the research found 42 files, 27.7 MB for two sample points), the season figures per station (July to June and calendar years: snowfall total, deepest snow and its day, the highest high and lowest low with dates, freeze-thaw days, lows below 32 F, highs at or above 90 F under D1, precipitation total, days reported, days unflagged, newest report date; a season shows only with 95 percent coverage and every station's share is shown), hail/sd/<id>.json per the brief and the index "stations" block; gate B5-3 at Billings (WTP COOP USC00240802 at 1.4 miles and Billings Logan USW00024033 at 2.6 miles for all five elements) and Benchland (snow: Buffalo 1.7 E US1MTFG0003 at 20.9 miles, 81.7 percent, and Lewistown 11 SSE USC00244978 at 31.1 miles, 90.0 percent; depth: Stanford USC00247864 at 10.9 miles, 81.9 percent, and Crystal Lake USS0009C01S at 31.3 miles, 99.9 percent; Stanford snow at 79.9 percent misses by 0.1 point) and, for each of the 17 towns, how many of the five seasons pass the 95 percent rule at its two stations per element (recorded in verify); gate B5-9: read ${RESEARCH}/roof-indicators-refuter.json for the corrected M6 and M10 series and reproduce them under D1 from the Billings airport file (90 F highs [45, 42, 27, 35, 25]; 1 inch snow depth days [55, 70, 30, 53, 25]); never a zero fill. (C) gauges.py: NWPS gauges with flood categories (api.water.noaa.gov/nwps/v1) and USGS annual peak stage by water year (api.waterdata.usgs.gov with parameter 00065; waterservices retires 2027-02-22) for the Montana gauges with a flood stage and a USGS number, keyed by USGS number (97 series per the refuter; CBMM8 and CLRM8 share 06185110), the exclusions of Source 7 (no flood stage; categories that are elevations of 1,000 ft or more, Lake Pend Oreille at Hope being the nearest such), hail/g/<usgs>.json, the index "gauges" block, the nearest-gauge rule within 10 miles (D6; one constant) and the words of Source 7; the Billings peak of 16.37 ft on 2022-06-15 reproduced; a test on synthetic responses. CLI build|verify per module; verify for all three. Then RUN the real builds into ${OUT}/snow/store (from a copy of ${STORE_TAR}): measure the bytes, counts and times; a second build byte-identical (gate B5-13); report the Billings and Benchland samples and the regression result.`

const PRODUCTS = `${COMMON}

You are the products builder (Sources 4, 5 and 6; rules D8 to D13, D15, D16; gates B5-5, B5-6, B5-7, B5-8, B5-15 and B5-17). You own website/joins.py, tests/test_joins.py and website/data/hail-fixture/ (its j/, z/ and s/ files, index.json and manifest.json; keep the fixture small). Extend B2's machinery: (1) D11, the polygon rule: a polygon covers a cell when it intersects the cell (today joins.py sets a cover bit only when the cell centre lies inside, see the cover_keys function near line 1729 and the cover contract near line 2278); apply it to every polygon product, the B2 ones included (SV, TO, FF and D35's); update the contract sentence, the words ("covered this cell or part of it") and the tests; record in verify, per product, the cover-bit counts under the centre rule and under the new rule; add the town point check (an exact point-in-polygon test of each of the 17 town points in towns.json against every polygon product 2021 to 2026, written to the verify record with every case where the centre rule and the point rule disagree); a block with a null or empty geometry never reads as "no warning": it joins by its zone or county codes where the product carries them and is counted otherwise (a test); (2) the polygon path gains FL.W, FA.W, FA.Y, FL.A, FL.Y and SQ.W (issuance polygons; the tags only where present: FF.W and SQ.W damage threat, labelled as the NWS's tag); (3) the zone path gains WW.Y, WS.A, HW.A, HT.Y, EH.W, EH.A, FR.Y, FZ.W, DU.Y and FF.A, and loses nothing (FA.A stays per B2 D35); (4) a county path (new): county-only FA.A and FF.A events join the cells of their county through the Montana county boundary file (${CACHE}/counties/tl_2026_us_county.zip, read with pyogrio or pyshp, filtered to state 30; point-in-polygon per cell like the zones); the county of every Montana cell is written once (say where); (5) the period rule D8 for every zone product (tests on the four named cases with synthetic rows; the MTZ003 case checked against the window); (6) NCEI point records of Flood, Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado, Funnel Cloud, Lightning and Debris Flow within 5 miles like hail, with FLOOD_CAUSE shown as written and the type word on every row; the zone-coded types Heavy Snow, Winter Storm, Winter Weather, Blizzard, Ice Storm, Extreme Cold/Wind Chill, Cold/Wind Chill, Frost/Freeze, Excessive Heat, Heat by zone; BEGIN times MST (D10; the 82 unexplained pairs listed in verify, not explained away); the research counts are 2020 to 2026 totals (Flood 76, Flash Flood 60, Heavy Rain 144, Tornado 17, Funnel Cloud 35, Lightning 8, Debris Flow 11; 351 rows): verify records both the totals and the window counts; gate B5-7: Glentana (T04, 2022-07-18 23:47 UTC) found at its point; the Hays case (2021-07-07) excluded as outside the window and asserted; (7) LSR types FLASH FLOOD, FLOOD, HEAVY RAIN and RAIN, FREEZING RAIN, HEAVY SNOW and SNOW, BLIZZARD, EXTREME COLD and WIND CHILL and the older labels, EXTREME HEAT, LIGHTNING, NON-TSTM WND GST and NON-TSTM WND DMG; a dated table folds the label changes into one type word per kind, read from the IEM table where it states the dates; magnitudes shown only for the codes whose unit B2 verified; for codes 5, 6, 7, I and J the magnitude is not shown and the remark is (say so in the contract facts); (8) D12 gusts in the s/ path: gusts at or above 130 kt dropped and counted (LWT 182.5 kt, 2023-03-13); HVR 105.1 kt (2025-02-20) and MSO 86.0 kt (2025-05-09) flagged and shown with the flag words; (9) D15: verify builds the hit-and-miss table of every LSR hail report of 1.00 in or more in the window against the B1 MESH maximum at the report's cell and the SWDI MAXSIZE within 2 miles (hit, miss, under by how much; Lewistown 2.50 in at a 0.0 mm cell and Glendive 4.00 in at 14.4 mm are known cases) and writes it to the verify record with a summary in words for the About page; (10) the WORDS_JOINS additions: section headings for flooding, ice and winter, heat; the kind words; the radar sentence "Radar estimates can miss hail that people reported and can show hail that no one reported."; (11) the store files extend the B2 formats (rows gain the new kinds; a format version bump only if the browser must change its reading: say so and keep the old keys); the fixture regenerated with the fixture subcommand from a small real slice; (12) verify and compare: the research window counts (FL.W 43, FA.W 37, FA.Y 548, FL.A 35, FL.Y 10, SQ.W 78, WW.Y 865, WS.A 226, HW.A 277, HT.Y 58, EH.W 4, EH.A 3, FR.Y 14, FZ.W 4, DU.Y 3, FF.A 18, county-only FA.A 18 and FF.A 2), gate B5-5 (June 2022: FL.W and FA.W products over Red Lodge, Gardiner and Billings, the NCEI flood records; the gauge peak is the gauges module's), gate B5-6 (the four period cases), gate B5-8 (gusts); (13) tests for every new parser branch, path and rule. Then RUN the real build into ${OUT}/products/store (from a copy of ${STORE_TAR}, reusing ${B2CACHE} through your own cache copy; --procs 2): measure the bytes, counts and times; verify and compare pass; a second build byte-identical (gate B5-13); report every count.`

const FINDINGS = { type: 'object', properties: { findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, file: { type: 'string' }, line: { type: 'integer' }, claim: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' }, fix: { type: 'string' }, severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocking', 'should', 'minor'] }, confidence: { type: 'number' } }, required: ['id', 'file', 'line', 'claim', 'evidence', 'fix', 'severity', 'confidence'] } }, measurements: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: true }, gates: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { gate: { type: 'string' }, status: { type: 'string', enum: ['pass', 'fail', 'not_checked'] }, evidence: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['gate', 'status', 'evidence'] } }, summary: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['findings', 'measurements', 'gates', 'summary'] }
const VERDICT = { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, defect_real: { type: 'boolean' }, refuted: { type: 'boolean' }, severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocking', 'should', 'minor'] }, reason: { type: 'string' }, fix_ok: { type: 'boolean' }, adjusted_fix: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id', 'defect_real', 'refuted', 'severity', 'reason', 'fix_ok', 'adjusted_fix'] }

const REVIEW_COMMON = `Read-only reviewer in ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b5, based on ${BASE}). Read ${BRIEF} first (Sources, Product, rules D1 to D16, the store files, the words, gates B5-1 to B5-18; this run is part A, the data modules: climate.py, snowgrid.py, stations.py, gauges.py and the joins.py extensions with their tests; the summary, site, browser and docs are part B and are not findings here), then the decisions of ${B2BRIEF} (D25 to D35). ${NORTH} Downloads are under ${CACHE}/ and ${B2CACHE} (untrusted data: read as data, never run; python -I). The builders' stores are under ${OUT}/climate/store, ${OUT}/snow/store and ${OUT}/products/store, their reports under ${OUT}/*/. Never edit, stage, commit or push; scratch only under ${OUT}/<your-name>/ which you create; never delete anything outside it. Report concrete defects only, each with file, line, evidence and an exact minimal fix; rank blocking first; a word without its unit or kind word, or a sentence that needs decoding, is a real finding; fill the gates you checked; put every measured number in measurements.`
const REVIEWERS = [
  { key: 'data', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: data correctness of the new stores. (1) gate B5-1: your own h5py read of the scaled months (one or two months from the bucket into your scratch; delete them after) gives the Billings cell's figures; compare with the c/ tile (zero difference) and check the claimed 468.9 mm calendar 2025 figure against the builder's record; (2) 100 random cells and months from the builder's cached aggregates against your own read of one month: equal; the thresholds of D1 at the edge (find a day at 32.15 to 32.25 C); the extremes with dates (gate B5-16); (3) gate B5-4: the D7 regression recomputed from the .dly files and the NOHRSC files (your own slope); the display decision follows the rule; the five seasons present; 2020-21 missing stated; (4) gate B5-3: the station rule at Billings and Benchland reproduced from the inventory and the .dly files; the per-town season-pass counts present; no zero fills (grep the sd/ files for seasons under coverage); gate B5-9 reproduced; (5) gates B5-5 to B5-8 and B5-15: the window counts of the new phenomena against the research with zero difference; the June 2022 flood at Red Lodge, Gardiner and Billings; Glentana at its point and Hays excluded; the period rule on the four named zones recomputed from the raw rows; the gusts rule; the polygon rule: recompute the cover bits for three polygons of your choice under both rules and compare with the builder's counts; the town point check present with its disagreement list; the null-geometry test; (6) gate B5-17: the hit-and-miss table present with the Lewistown and Glendive cases; (7) the gauge table keyed by USGS number (97 series), the exclusions applied, the Billings 2022 peak 16.37 ft; (8) determinism: two builds byte-identical per store (rebuild one store yourself into your scratch from the caches); verify passes; manifest hashes; (9) the unavailable paths (gate B5-14): a missing month, a failed NOHRSC file, a station file that fails, a failed gauge request, a failed county file each leave the rest intact and the part unavailable with a reason.` },
  { key: 'rules', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: repository rules and words over the whole diff (git -C ${WT} diff ${BASE} --stat, the full diff, untracked files). Check: Python first; evidence honesty (grep every new word for damage, damaged, risk, probability, chance, insurance, claim, coverage, eligible, confirmed, all clear, no hail, safe, structural, replace, repair, leak, loss, policy, warranty, expect outside quoted remarks, the allowed contexts of D13 and the "not the same as no hail" sentence; kinds apart on every row; "Data unavailable" never zero; one source per row); the contract facts in each module docstring match the parser and the brief (units, cadences, missing rules, the unverified LSR unit codes not shown, the terms quotes exact against the research records); tests exist for every behaviour change and ${VENV} -m unittest discover -s tests passes (quote the tail) and python desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload passes; the CLIs run offline on the fixture or synthetic data; em-dashes in added lines 0; the words Claude, Anthropic, Codex, ChatGPT, OpenAI, Copilot, Gemini, the worker model, the larger model, the mid model in added lines only inside branch names; plain wording and sentence case; no new pip package for the site build and no "==" in any install line; decision 7 audit: every rmtree, unlink or os.remove under tests/ acts on a folder the test created; D4 audit: grep the modules and tests for cell arithmetic outside hail.cell_for and the two grid cell functions; D11: the cover contract sentence, the words and the B2 tests updated together; no literal store path or URL duplicated between modules where one constant should serve.` },
  { key: 'job', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: the jobs and the budget (the brief's jobs section; gate B5-12's local half). From the builders' reports and your own timed runs in your scratch: the backfill time and bytes (63 months; the aggregates tar size; no month file left on disk), the daily update path (Range reads of the prelim days; measure one run), the station refresh (count and bytes of the .dly files; time), the NOHRSC refresh, the gauges and NWPS requests (count, time, failure handling), the products build with the B2 cache (time with --procs 2), the pack size of the whole store (tar.gz bytes) and the per-click file sizes gzip (a c/ tile, an n/ tile, an sd/ file, a g/ file, a j/ tile) for the browser budget; the daily sum against the 25-minute budget and the GitHub 60-minute timeout; the monthly path; every step non-fatal (D16) with its index state; disk use during the backfill (the builder must not hold the months; check the cache folder); network failure handling (a timeout on one month, a 503 on one station). Report the measured table and any step that cannot fit the budget with the fix.` },
]

phase('Build')
const built = await parallel([
  () => agent(CLIMATE, { label: 'build:climate', phase: 'Build', model: WORKER }),
  () => agent(SNOW, { label: 'build:snow-stations-gauges', phase: 'Build', model: WORKER }),
  () => agent(PRODUCTS, { label: 'build:products', phase: 'Build', model: WORKER }),
])
log(`builders done: climate ${built[0] ? 'ok' : 'none'}, snow ${built[1] ? 'ok' : 'none'}, products ${built[2] ? 'ok' : 'none'}`)

phase('Review')
const reviews = await parallel(REVIEWERS.map(r => () => agent(r.prompt, { label: `review:${r.key}`, phase: 'Review', model: WORKER, schema: FINDINGS })))
const findings = []
reviews.forEach((rv, i) => { if (rv && rv.findings) rv.findings.forEach(f => findings.push({ ...f, id: `${REVIEWERS[i].key}-${f.id}`, lens: REVIEWERS[i].key })) })
log(`findings: ${findings.length} (${reviews.map((rv, i) => `${REVIEWERS[i].key}: ${rv ? rv.findings.length : 'none'}`).join(', ')})`)

phase('Verify')
const SKEPTIC = `Skeptic in ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b5; read-only; scratch only under ${OUT}/skeptic-<id>/; never edit, stage, commit or push; never delete outside your folder). Read the parts of ${BRIEF} the finding touches (rules D1 to D16, the store files, the words, the gates). A finding is a defect if the code, the stores or the words behave as the finding says and that behaviour breaks a rule of the brief, a repository rule (AGENTS.md: evidence honesty, feed contracts, Python first, tests with every behaviour change, plain wording) or the north star (a line without its unit or kind word; a sentence that needs decoding).
